name: Hua Wei
title: Assistant Professor; Data Mining and Reinforcement Learning Group
department: School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence
fitReason: A direct visitor inquiry route plus verified small-scale physical robot learning; broader lab work spans reinforcement learning, transportation and trustworthy AI.

physicalEvidence.summary: A 2025 FURI primary poster supervised by Wei shows actual miniature-vehicle lane-keeping, a real-world map and explicit policy-deployment loop. It compares behavior cloning and implicit Q-learning using simulated, real and mixed demonstrations. Full poster rendering verifies the physical setup. Results are preliminary: the poster calls differences negligible and leaves intersection maneuvers/pedestrian avoidance to future work; no strong improvement or safety claim is made. A February 2026 ASU report independently confirms the project, actual vehicles and Wei’s supervision. This establishes current-host learned execution at prototype scale, not full-size road deployment. DADiff/Found-adapt and PlantShade remain simulation/data work and are not counted as newer physical robot experiments.

shortVisit.summary: Current official prospective-student page explicitly welcomes self-funded visiting students/scholars, while separately describing ASU-enrolled master’s and PhD recruitment. Lab homepage also advertises flexible-time research interns. These are inquiry invitations without confirmed summer 2027 dates, eight-week duration, funding or acceptance.
